name: stereotype
description: The Spring stereotype of the subject type, a bean class: controller, service, repository, configuration or component, the most specific its annotations carry, directly or through meta-annotations. A Jakarta REST resource (a class with @Path, on it or a supertype) is a controller.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation written on the type that makes it one, such as a custom annotation carrying @RestController.

via.description: The meta-annotations leading from that annotation to the stereotype, in order. Absent when the stereotype is written directly.

rest.description: Present and true for a controller whose handler methods write their response to the body (@RestController or @ResponseBody), or a Jakarta REST resource.

name: main-class
description: The subject type is an application's main class: spring-boot for a Spring Boot application class (@SpringBootApplication or @EnableAutoConfiguration, directly or through meta-annotations), java for another class with a main(String[]) method.

main.description: The entity ID of the type's main(String[]) method. Absent for a Spring Boot application class without one.

name: entry-point
description: The subject method is where work starts in a running application, such as a request handler, a scheduled job or a message listener. Its subtypes say which kind. Values resolved from config are those of the default view unless profile is set.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one when the value was resolved. Absent for the default view; present only where the value differs from it.

written.description: The value as written in the code, when it differs from the resolved value (it had placeholders).

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders no config value resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a placeholder named a secret, so the value is recorded as written, not resolved.

name: endpoint
description: The subject method handles HTTP requests: the HTTP method and path, such as POST /api/orders, or the path alone when it takes any method. The path joins the controller's and the method's mappings, with placeholders resolved against the config of the controller's module; linking records it from the HANDLED_BY fact of the http-endpoint (ADR 0094, #519).

httpMethod.description: The HTTP method, such as GET. Absent when the mapping takes any method.

controller.description: The binary name of the controller class, which differs from the method's own type when the method is inherited.

annotation.description: The binary name of the mapping annotation on the method, such as org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping.

framework.description: Which annotations map the request: Spring MVC or WebFlux request mappings, or Jakarta (or javax) REST.

name: scheduled
description: The subject method runs on a schedule (@Scheduled, JobRunr's @Recurring or a request scheduled recurrently, or a Quartz job whose cron was found): the cron expression, or the delay or rate, with placeholders resolved against the config of the method's module; for @Scheduled and @Recurring linking records it from the scheduled-written fact (ADR 0094, #519).

timeUnit.description: The unit of a delay or rate when written, such as SECONDS. Milliseconds when absent.

framework.description: The job library, for a job of JobRunr or Quartz. Absent for @Scheduled.

request.description: A JobRunr request handler's request type, the binary name.

job.description: A Quartz job's class, the binary name.

scheduledBy.description: The IDs of the methods whose code sets the job up: passes its request to the scheduler, or builds its Quartz job and trigger. Absent when none is found in the analyzed code.

name: background-job
description: The subject method runs as a background job that a library starts, not on a cron, delay or rate: a JobRunr request handler's run method (the job runs when its request is enqueued or scheduled once), an @Job method, a @Recurring interval, or a Quartz job whose cron was not found. The value is the job's name, interval or class.

kind.description: What the value is: the job (its @Job name, its request type or its Quartz class), or a @Recurring interval.

request.description: A JobRunr request handler's request type, the binary name.

job.description: A Quartz job's class, the binary name.

scheduledBy.description: The IDs of the methods whose code sets the job up: passes its request to the scheduler, or builds its Quartz job and trigger. Absent when none is found in the analyzed code.

name: profile-gate
description: The subject bean class or @Bean method is only registered when the profile expression matches the active profiles (@Profile, directly or through a meta-annotation), such as audit, !prod or (a) | (b) for several.

profiles.description: The profile expressions as written; any one matching is enough.

annotation.description: The binary name of the custom annotation carrying @Profile, when it is not written directly.

name: bean
description: The subject method defines a Spring bean (@Bean); the value is the bean's name, the first name the annotation gives or else the method's name.

name: aspect
description: The subject type is an AspectJ aspect (an @Aspect class) with advice (@Before, @After, @AfterReturning, @AfterThrowing, @Around). It runs around the methods its pointcuts select, which ADVISES lists; an aspect that enforces access (a permission or membership check) is a component of the units whose entry points it advises.

advice.description: The kinds of advice the aspect has: before, after, after-returning, after-throwing, around.

pointcuts.description: The pointcut expressions of its advice, as written.

annotations.description: The binary names of the annotations its pointcuts select methods or types by (@annotation, @within, @target), such as a permission annotation. Absent when none.

name: ADVISES
description: The subject aspect's advice selects the object method: the aspect runs around its calls. Read from the advice's pointcut (@annotation, @within, @target, within and execution designators, and named pointcuts) against the methods of the analyzed code, including other repositories.

advice.description: The entity ID of the advice method.

name: property-gate
description: The subject bean class or @Bean method is only registered when the properties named have the value given (@ConditionalOnProperty, directly or through a meta-annotation). The value is the properties joined by & and, when given, =havingValue.

properties.description: The full property keys, the prefix joined to each name.

havingValue.description: The value the properties must have; absent when any value but false will do.

matchIfMissing.description: Present and true when the bean is registered also when the property is not set.

annotation.description: The binary name of the custom annotation carrying @ConditionalOnProperty, when it is not written directly.

name: discovery-client
description: The subject main class registers its unit with service discovery (@EnableDiscoveryClient or the older @EnableEurekaClient). A unit also registers with no annotation, through a discovery client starter alone; joining the two is the linker's. The value is discovery.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation.

autoRegister.description: Present and false when the annotation turns registration off.

name: infrastructure-server
description: The subject main class makes its unit an infrastructure server: a Eureka server (@EnableEurekaServer), a config server (@EnableConfigServer) or a Spring Boot Admin server (@EnableAdminServer). The value is eureka, config or admin.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation.

name: access-check
description: Callers of the subject method, or of every method of the subject class, must pass the access check its method security annotation states: @PreAuthorize, @PostAuthorize, @Secured, @RolesAllowed, @PermitAll or @DenyAll, directly or through a meta-annotation. The value is the expression or roles as written, else the kind. It is enforced only where method security is on (method-security). With via aspect (#520), the check is a custom one an aspect makes instead: its before or around advice applies to the method because of the annotation at this line, and reads that annotation's attributes; the value is the annotation's values as written, such as resource=TASK, action=READ, and the check is enforced wherever the aspect is a bean.

kind.description: The kind of check: custom for one an aspect makes.

annotation.description: The binary name of the custom annotation carrying the check, when it is not written directly; for via aspect, the annotation the aspect reads.

via.description: aspect when an aspect makes the check (#520); absent for method security.

aspect.description: For via aspect: the aspect's binary name.

advice.description: For via aspect: the entity ID of the advice method that makes the check.

name: method-security
description: The subject class turns method security on for the units that load it (@EnableMethodSecurity, @EnableReactiveMethodSecurity or the older @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity), so access-check annotations of the kinds it enables are enforced. The value is on.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation.

name: advised-by
description: An aspect's advice applies to the subject method because of the annotation at this line, which its pointcut selects by @annotation, @within or @target, such as a custom permission check. The value is the aspect's binary name. The ADVISES relation states the same from the aspect's side, at the advice.

advice.description: The entity ID of the advice method.

annotation.description: The binary name of the selecting annotation.

name: SCHEDULES
description: The subject method schedules the object job method (JobRunr or Quartz) at the call this fact cites. The job's own fact names its schedulers as scheduledBy.

name: http-endpoint
description: An HTTP endpoint a module's code serves, as the code writes it (ADR 0094, #519): the module's key, ':', the HTTP method or * when the mapping takes any, ':' and the path as written, the controller's and the method's joined, with their placeholders, such as com.acme:orders:POST:/api/orders or com.acme:orders:GET:${api.prefix}/orders. Linking resolves its path in each view and records the endpoint facts. (The endpoint attribute type, which documents read until #521, keeps that name.)

name: HANDLED_BY
description: The subject endpoint is handled by the object method, at the mapping this fact cites. Its paths are as written; linking resolves them in each view against the config of configModule (ADR 0094, #519).

httpMethod.description: The HTTP method, such as POST. Absent when the mapping takes any.

basePath.description: The controller's path as written, empty when it has none.

path.description: The method's path as written, empty when it has none.

controller.description: The binary name of the controller class.

annotation.description: The binary name of the mapping annotation written on the method.

framework.description: spring-mvc or jakarta-rest, as for endpoint.

configModule.description: The entity ID of the module whose config resolves the paths: the code's.

name: scheduled-written
description: The subject method runs on a schedule written so in code (@Scheduled, or JobRunr's @Recurring with a cron): the cron, delay or rate as written, with its placeholders. Linking resolves it in each view against the config of configModule and records the scheduled facts (ADR 0094, #519).

timeUnit.description: The time unit written for a delay or rate.

framework.description: jobrunr for a @Recurring method; absent for Spring's @Scheduled.

configModule.description: The entity ID of the module whose config resolves the value: the code's.

name: reads-request-value
description: The subject method reads a value of the HTTP request it serves (#520): a header, cookie or parameter, bound to a parameter of a handler (@RequestHeader, @CookieValue or @RequestParam, or Jakarta REST's @HeaderParam, @CookieParam or @QueryParam, also when written on the method it overrides), or read by a call on the request in any code, such as a filter, an aspect or an interceptor (a servlet request's getHeader, a reactive request's getHeaders().getFirst). The value is the name as written, constants folded and a @Value's text kept; for a binding without a name, the parameter's name, or * for a map of every value.

source.description: What is read: a header, a cookie, or a request parameter (query or form).

via.description: binding for a handler's parameter, call for a call on the request.

annotation.description: For a binding: the binary name of the binding annotation.

parameter.description: For a binding: the parameter's name.

call.description: For a call: the name of the method that reads the value, such as getHeader or getFirst.

requestType.description: For a call: the binary name of the request type the call chain starts from.

name: transactional
description: The subject method, or every method of the subject type, runs in a transaction (#520), as @Transactional states (Spring's, or Jakarta's), directly or through a meta-annotation: the value is the propagation as written, else REQUIRED. Or, with kind event-listener, the subject method listens for application events at a phase of the publishing transaction (@TransactionalEventListener): the value is the phase as written, else AFTER_COMMIT.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation written.

readOnly.description: Spring's readOnly as written, when it is.

name: cors-policy
description: A CORS policy (#520): the origins a browser may call the subject from, as written (or, from config, as resolved), joined by a comma and a space. From code, the subject is the controller or handler of a @CrossOrigin (every origin when it names none), or the method that makes a CorsConfiguration or registers a mapping with a web configurer's CorsRegistry. From config (the Config extractor), the subject is the module whose Spring Cloud Gateway global CORS or Actuator CORS keys set it. From a Kubernetes Ingress's nginx annotations (the Deployment extractor), the subject is the repository.

origins.description: The allowed origins or origin patterns, each as written.

credentials.description: Whether credentials are allowed, as written, when it is.

path.description: The path pattern the policy applies to, when one is written.

key.description: From config: the key that sets the origins.

written.description: From config: the origins as written, when they differ from the resolved value.

profile.description: From config: the profile active instead of the default one, present only where the policy differs from the default view's.

platform.description: From an Ingress: the platform, as for deployment-route.

environment.description: From an Ingress: the environment, as for deployment-route.
